name: Charcot-Marie-Tooth Disease Type 2

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Electrophysiological Diagnostic Criteria for CMT

criteria.description: Presence of distal muscle weakness and atrophy predominantly in the lower limbs
Distal sensory loss including reduced vibration and proprioception
Electrophysiological evidence of axonal neuropathy with normal or mildly reduced nerve conduction velocities
Positive family history consistent with autosomal dominant inheritance
Identification of pathogenic variants in genes associated with CMT2 (e.g., MFN2, MPZ)

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of distal muscle weakness and sensory loss with electrophysiological evidence of axonal neuropathy
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic testing can confirm diagnosis but is not mandatory.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Reduced or absent deep tendon reflexes

laboratory: Elevated creatine kinase levels may be mild or absent
imaging: MRI may show muscle atrophy in distal limbs
genetic: Pathogenic variants in MFN2, MPZ, GJB1, and other CMT2-associated genes
other: Nerve conduction studies showing reduced compound muscle action potential amplitudes with normal or mildly reduced conduction velocities

distinguishingFeatures: Demyelinating neuropathy with markedly reduced nerve conduction velocities
Recurrent focal neuropathies at entrapment sites
Usually normal nerve conduction velocities between episodes
Distinct clinical course with episodic symptoms

redFlags: Rapidly progressive weakness or sensory loss
references: Pareyson D, Marchesi C. Diagnosis, natural history, and management of Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease. Lancet Neurol. 2009;8(7):654-667.
Saporta MA, Shy ME. Inherited peripheral neuropathies. Neurol Clin. 2013;31(2):597-619.
Lupski JR. Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease: a new paradigm for the molecular genetics of inherited disease. Mol Med Today. 1997;3(8):342-349.
